headline: Sequence models and count-based eQTL methods are tested for individual-level expression effects
label: Donor Aware Expression Modeling
summary: New sc-eQTL count models, uncertainty-aware prediction and stress tests of sequence models bear on how variant effects are inferred across individuals and cell types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is modeling genetic effects on expression at the individual and cell-type level with methods matched to the data. SAIGE-QTL and jaxQTL replace linear sc-eQTL models with Poisson mixed and negative binomial count models, reporting better calibration, scalability or eGene discovery. ATTICUS pairs personalised sequence representations with uncertainty-aware prediction for cell-type TWAS, and RSparsePro targets fine-mapping under LD reference mismatch. A second strand evaluates sequence-based predictors: AlphaGenome promoter perturbations show decoupled CAGE and RNA-seq outputs, ChromBPNet scores noncoding variants across hematopoietic lineages, ModBERT adds variants and CpG methylation to a DNA language model, and Evo2VED releases precomputed Evo2 scores for gnomAD variants. The items are adjacent rather than a single pipeline.
